To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DGFF is a conformally invariant random field, in the sense of a scaling limit.

the scaling limit of the level sets of the DGFF is LQG; the law of the field values at the points of the level set is that of an exponential measure; and the law of the reduced configuration is that of a pinned DGF reduced by a suitable version of the potential kernel.
the DGFF is a conformal field theory, and the LQG theory of a conformal field with a non-zero central charge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the scaling limit of a typical point on an intermediate level set of the DGFF.
the scaling limit of the DGFF in a continuum domain, and the local structure of the level sets.
the scaling limit, in a certain regime, of the intermediate level sets of the DGFF, which are the natural analogues of the level sets of the Gaussian Free Field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DGFF in $D$ has a scaling limit that is a LQG measure with the law of a DGFF pinned to the LQG interface.
the scaling limit of the DGFF level set is a pinned DGFF, with the pinning potential given by the $\lambda$-quantile of the LQGF measure.
the scaling limit of the level set is a LQG measure with a random height field.
